contests.title: Broward County — Health care services sales surtax

provenance.sourceOrg: Broward County Board of County Commissioners
provenance.quote: Shall Broward County fund (1) preventive heart and cancer tests, to the extent not covered by insurance, for qualified Broward County residents, (2) primary and preventive health care for indigent or medically poor residents, and (3) other health services, as described in a County health care plan, as periodically amended, by levying a one quarter of one percent sales surtax for five years subject to automatic repeal if a 1% infrastructure surtax is levied?

contests.title: Broward County — Alternative process for plat approval

provenance.sourceOrg: Broward County Board of County Commissioners
provenance.quote: Currently under the Broward County Charter, all plats in Broward County must be approved by the County Commission prior to recording; this proposal amends the Charter to allow the County Commission to provide, by ordinance, as permitted under state law, an alternative process for approving plats, such as administrative approval, which might enable more expeditious plat approval including by allowing approval when the County Commission is in recess.

provenance.sourceOrg: Broward County Board of County Commissioners
provenance.quote: Currently under the Broward County Charter, an independent board nominates one individual for County Auditor, and the County Commission ratifies that selection upon determining the nominee is qualified. Should the Charter be amended to provide that the independent board nominates three individuals, thereby enabling the County Commission to appoint as County Auditor the qualified nominee it determines is best able to serve in that position?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 0.25% sales surtax for five years to fund the County Health Care Plan, which the county may periodically amend. It would fund preventive heart and cancer tests for qualified county residents to the extent insurance does not cover them, primary and preventive care for indigent or medically poor residents, and other services described in the plan. The surtax would automatically end if a one-percent infrastructure surtax is levied.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the five-year 0.25% health-care sales surtax, with the stated services and automatic-repeal condition.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed health-care sales surtax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the County Commission to adopt an ordinance setting an alternative process for approving land-division maps, called plats, consistent with state law. That could include approval by county staff instead of requiring the Commission to approve every plat before recording it. Voter approval would allow a later ordinance; it would not itself create a particular alternative approval process.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve allowing the County Commission to establish alternative plat-approval methods by ordinance, consistent with state law.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to the Charter’s Commission-approval requirement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the independent board’s role from nominating one county-auditor candidate to nominating three. The County Commission would choose one by majority vote, after determining the person is qualified. The auditor must maintain an active Florida public-accounting license and have sufficient government accounting and auditing experience, and serves a five-year term. The three-candidate selection process also applies to vacancies; an interim appointment remains limited to 90 days.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the three-candidate nomination process and majority-vote Commission appointment of a qualified county auditor.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to the county-auditor selection process.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews the one-mill school property tax for January 1, 2027, through December 31, 2030. It funds safety and security staff, mental-health professionals, teacher and eligible-staff compensation, and essential instructional expenses for traditional public and charter schools. Collections would support fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2031. The School Board could repeal or reduce the levy earlier by resolution without another referendum. Monthly receipt and spending reports would be posted on the Board’s website.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve renewing the one-mill school property tax for the stated period and purposes, with public monthly reports and the Board’s power to reduce or repeal it earlier.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed renewal of the one-mill school property tax.
